answer: A sponsor quota blocks rented identities. Each newcomer needs a sponsor who locks a non-transferable bond and may vouch for five newcomers at most under an unpoolable cap. The applicant files a sample whose juniper tag, from its key and task, is recorded on the reef ledger. Auditors match tag to key at dawn; a rented sample fails and its bond is slashed. The k-th fake costs 35+0.09k^2 units, rising with n: each fake needs a fresh bond, slot, and tag; 1,000 fakes cost 30,080,015 units. Device farms fail: quota is unbuyable, tags unreusable. Honest agents pay once.
